observations: Godin & Thivierge PLOS Computational Biology 2026 still exposes S1 Code as a ZIP, but the current read-only transport again did not yield file-level contents; no mutation or probe side effect was used.

Schwarcz et al. PLOS Computational Biology 2025 showed mice adapting on the first trial after latent context shifts without reward feedback, derived a Bayes-optimal sequential belief-state policy, and found recurrent neural networks learned Bayesian-inference-like dynamics. This supports uncertainty/context-belief gating as a plausible computational motif, but does not validate the present duration controller.

bounded_audit.scope: Synthetic bounded causal control continuing the prior permutation/duration-hypothesis audit. Not an exact reproduction of SPLiT or a neuroscience experiment.

design.event_duration_model: Discrete geometric durations; normal regime mean duration S=6/C=16 and swapped regime S=16/C=6.
design.semantic_mapping: Two mapping hypotheses for observed prototype-track label to semantic cause, with a higher mapping-permutation hazard near a prototype-crossing window and sparse noisy semantic cues. Cue-loss scenarios remove semantic cues for a 200-event window.

controllers.two_hypothesis: Mapping-permutation filter with one fixed duration regime.
controllers.always_joint: Four joint hypotheses = mapping assignment x duration regime, active at all times.
controllers.hybrid_guarded: Two-hypothesis mapping filter by default. A decayed clipped posterior-predictive log Bayes factor compares the alternative versus current duration regime. Warning threshold=3.5 tempers stale duration likelihood to exponent 0.4; full joint mode activates at score>6 for 3 consecutive events and collapses after high posterior confidence. Explicit label-symmetry abstention maps to 0.5 when both mapping and regime identity are weak.

design.calibration: Guard thresholds were chosen on disjoint small stable-regime calibration streams, then frozen before held-out evaluation; stable-regime verification showed low warning/activation occupancy.
design.heldout_semantic_eval: 96 paired seeds per scenario, 800 events/seed; paired bootstrap 95% intervals over seed-level Brier differences.
design.memory_controller: Posterior-driven dormant-direction restore on a circular one-dimensional tracking task. Fast PAST/GROUSE-like tracker eta=0.25; slow Oja-like tracker eta=0.06. Memory restore uses the pre-event direction. Previous role-local threshold 0.97 was too permissive under mixed shifts, so a separately checked ultra-conservative fast policy uses P(silence)>0.99995 and restore blend=0.6; slow-memory policy is retained as disabled/no-restore after direct testing. Memory evaluation uses 80 paired seeds for the final fast policy.

fast_policy.rule: restore only when hybrid posterior P(temporary-silence)>0.99995; blend=0.6
fast_policy.interpretation: Ultra-conservative restore produces small but resolved post-silence recovery gains while no persistent-change harm is resolved. The effect is far smaller than the earlier permissive restore because only ~3-4% of true silence events are admitted.

slow_policy.evidence: With P(silence)>0.99995 and blend=0.2, slow-tracker memory had no resolved matched benefit and significantly worsened overall error under duration-swap and mixed conditions; the slow base tracker already carries sufficient inertia.

mechanistic_interpretation.positive: A hierarchical controller can avoid the permanent uncertainty cost of always carrying duration-regime hypotheses while still detecting true duration-semantic changes. A low-cost warning stage that tempers stale duration evidence substantially reduces the detection-window damage. Tracker-specific memory is possible, but only at extremely high semantic confidence for the fast tracker.
mechanistic_interpretation.negative_boundary: Always-joint inference remains materially better after a real duration-regime change; the current hybrid still pays 56-148 events of detection delay. Conversely, always-joint is worse under stable cue loss. This is an explicit adaptability-versus-baseline-complexity tradeoff rather than a universal winner. Slow trackers should not receive dormant-memory restoration, and permissive fast restoration creates stale interference under mixed shifts.
mechanistic_interpretation.identifiability: The prior permutation-symmetry boundary remains: when semantic mapping and duration labels are jointly observationally symmetric without independent cues, the controller must abstain rather than infer a semantic label from duration alone.

limits: Synthetic binary cause labels, geometric durations, known approximate prototype-crossing window, and simple circular subspace tracking.
The posterior-predictive score is a hand-designed Bayes-factor accumulator; it is not yet a fully online learned change-point model.
Prior shift is not separately modeled by the hybrid controller; the mixed scenario is therefore intentionally adversarial.
The final fast-memory benefit is small because the no-harm criterion forces a very high admission threshold.
SPLiT S1 Code.zip remains unrecovered at file level.
bounded_audit.exact_next_action: Continue read-only SPLiT S1 Code.zip recovery without mutation. Replace the hand-designed duration-change accumulator with an online Bayesian change-point or posterior-predictive surprise model that can lower the 56-148-event activation delay without increasing stable/cue-loss false activation; use a learned or calibrated hazard and explicit hysteresis. Evaluate gradual duration drift, non-geometric/overdispersed durations, repeated regime switches, exact cue-loss/recovery transients, and prior shifts. Retain the ultra-conservative fast-tracker dormant-memory policy only if post-silence recovery remains improved and post-switch interference remains statistically unresolved across these harder regimes; keep slow Oja-like restore disabled unless a new positive-control regime demonstrates simultaneous benefit. Preserve explicit label-symmetry abstention, exact tested scope, CLEAN isolation, and a nonempty frontier.
